risks.title: Loss of exclusive index options listing and trading rights
risks.score_rationale: Listed first in risk summary with strong language ('material adverse effect'). Loss of exclusive rights to products like S&P 500 index options would directly impact majority of Options segment revenue and overall profitability. (score par défaut, à affiner)
risks.summary: The Company could lose exclusive rights to list and trade certain index options and futures products, particularly index options, significantly reducing market share and rentability.

risks.title: Intense price competition and product commoditization
risks.score_rationale: Described with strong language ('intense price competition', 'intensify'). Directly impacts transactional revenue across all segments, with derivatives products increasingly commoditized. (score par défaut, à affiner)
risks.summary: Increasing price competition from competitors and industry consolidation pressures CBOE to lower transaction fees and market data pricing, reducing margins and revenues.

risks.title: Economic, political, and geopolitical market conditions
risks.score_rationale: Listed in risk summary with multiple cited factors. Directly impacts trading volumes and market data revenues which are sensitive to market activity and volatility levels. (score par défaut, à affiner)
risks.summary: Adverse global economic, political, and geopolitical conditions can reduce demand for CBOE's products and services, resulting in lower trading and clearing volumes.

risks.title: Cybersecurity vulnerabilities and system failures
risks.score_rationale: Highlighted in risk summary with references to 'security vulnerabilities and breaches' and ability to 'accommodate trading and clearing volume without failure'. System failures are operationally critical for an exchange. (score par défaut, à affiner)
risks.summary: Security vulnerabilities or breaches in CBOE's trading and clearing systems could cause service disruptions, operational failures, or data compromises, damaging reputation and customer relationships.

risks.title: Regulatory and legislative changes
risks.score_rationale: Listed in risk summary ('legal and regulatory obligations', 'legislative or regulatory changes'). Broad impact on operations including market structure rules, tax regimes, and compliance costs. (score par défaut, à affiner)
risks.summary: Changes in regulations, market structure rules, or tax regimes could increase compliance costs and affect CBOE's revenue models and competitive positioning.

risks.title: Dependence on third-party service providers
risks.score_rationale: Listed in risk summary ('dependence on and exposure to risk from third parties'). Introduces operational and business continuity risks given CBOE's reliance on external vendors. (score par défaut, à affiner)
risks.summary: CBOE's dependence on third-party providers for critical services introduces operational risks and potential business continuity threats if vendors fail or underperform.

risks.title: Loss of key customers and trading volume declines
risks.score_rationale: Mentioned in risk summary ('loss of key customers or significant reduction in trading or clearing volumes'). Direct impact on transaction-based revenues which comprise majority of operating income. (score par défaut, à affiner)
risks.summary: Loss of major customers or significant declines in their trading volumes would directly reduce CBOE's transaction revenues and operating profitability.

company_description: Cboe Global Markets, Inc., through its subsidiaries, operates as a derivatives and securities exchange network that delivers cutting-edge trading, clearing, and investment solutions in the United States and internationally. It operates through five segments: Options, North American Equities, Europe and Asia Pacific, Futures, and Global FX. The Options segment includes options on market indices, as well as on the stocks of individual corporations and on trading solutions and products in multiple asset classes, including equities, derivatives, and FX, across North America, Europe, and Asia Pacific (ETPs), such as exchange-traded funds (ETFs) and exchange-traded notes (ETNs); and trading in listed options through a single system. The North American Equities segment comprising U.S. equities and ETP transaction services. This segment also includes listing services on Cboe Canada, ETP listings on BZX, the Cboe Global Markets, Inc. common stock listing, and applicable market data.
